newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares mixed in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares mixed in brisk trade.

text.p: Many Nigerian blue chip shares rose while breweries took another knock in brisk Wednesday trading, dealers said.
The all-share index had not been updated by 1900 (1800 GMT).
Shares in oil marketers kept to a steady upward trend, with Unipetrol rising 30 kobo to close at 34.85 naira.
Cadbury gained 11 kobo to touch 23.74 naira. Flour Mills of Nigeria rose 10 kobo to 9.20 naira. Nigerian Bottling Company closed 10 kobo higher at 26.50 naira.
West African Portland Cement gained 12 kobo to 28.40 naira, while Ashaka Cement was 10 kobo higher at 15.30 naira.
Conglomerate PZ Industries rose 30 kobo to 33.30 naira.
But in the same sector the run on CFAO shares persisted. They fell 28 kobo, the maximum five percent allowed in one day, to 5.40 naira
The Franco-Nigerian company has slipped after poor first quarter results.
Nigerian Breweries fell a further 30 kobo to 13.30 naira, despite reports that the it was acquiring the local franchise to bottle Schweppes soft drinks.
The company said earlier this year it would diversify into other beverages to offset losses resulting from a shrinking beer market.

Chemical and Allied Products fell 20 kobo to 8.20 naira. Premier Paints lost two kobo to 90 kobo. Nigerian Yeast and Alcohol Manufacturing Company dropped five kobo to 6.70 naira and Vitafoam three kobo to 5.32 naira.
